boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten named, campus-listed study environments centered in Bortz Library and its technology commons.

cards.entity_name: Bortz Library First-Floor Quiet Study Area
cards.title: First-Floor Quiet Study Area
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Set up here when you need a designated quiet zone. Bring independent work and keep conversations for a different library area.
cards.short_summary: A specifically designated quiet-study area below Bortz Library’s main lobby.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hampden-Sydney Tiger identifies the first floor below Bortz Library’s main lobby as a specifically designated quiet study area.
cards.source_title: The Hampden-Sydney Tiger: Quick Tips for Finals
cards.access_notes: Campus facilities are privately owned; follow College and library access policies.

cards.entity_name: Bortz Library Second-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Second-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Use this floor’s group rooms for shared coursework. Keep the group within the posted room capacity and verify availability before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Student group-study rooms on Bortz Library’s second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s event planning guide lists group study rooms on Bortz Library’s second and third floors, seating 4–10.
cards.access_notes: Seats 4–10; student-only usage after 6 p.m.; rooms may not be reserved on the College calendar.

cards.entity_name: Bortz Library Third-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.title: Third-Floor Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Bring a small project team here for collaborative work. Check room occupancy and plan around the restriction on calendar reservations.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor option for small collaborative sessions in Bortz Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s event planning guide lists group study rooms on Bortz Library’s second and third floors, seating 4–10.
cards.access_notes: Seats 4–10; student-only usage after 6 p.m.; rooms may not be reserved on the College calendar.

cards.title: duPont Room 200
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Use the tablet-arm seating and whiteboards to work through material with classmates. This room is limited to academic-related use.
cards.short_summary: A library room with presentation equipment, whiteboards, and 25 tablet-arm chairs.
cards.evidence_claim: The College lists duPont Room 200 with 25 tablet-arm chairs, an LCD projector, two dry-erase boards, a computer, and a lectern.
cards.access_notes: Not available for non-academic-related events; event requests go through the College calendar.

cards.title: Classroom 217
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Choose this classroom for a structured review session using its document camera, display, and whiteboards. Confirm availability before using it.
cards.short_summary: A 16-seat library classroom equipped for document and screen-based work.
cards.evidence_claim: The College lists Classroom 217 as seating 16 classroom-style and equipped with a DVD player, document camera, 81-inch TV, two dry-erase boards, and lectern.
cards.access_notes: Use is subject to College event-space procedures; food and drink are allowed under the guide’s stated conditions.

cards.title: Conference/Seminar Room 218
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Reserve this table-based setting for discussion-heavy coursework or presentation planning. Keep the session sized for its twelve-seat conference table.
cards.short_summary: A 12-seat conference-table room in Bortz Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s event planning guide lists Bortz Library Conference/Seminar Room 218 as seating 12 at a conference table.
cards.access_notes: Follow College event-space procedures; food and drink are allowed, with a table needed for a buffet.

cards.entity_name: Bortz Library Second-Floor Main Reading Area
cards.title: Second-Floor Main Reading Area
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Use the main reading area for focused reading or laptop work. For an organized event, obtain both College Events and Library Director approval.
cards.short_summary: A named Bortz Library reading area with special approval requirements for events.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s event planning guide identifies the Second Floor Main Reading Area in Bortz Library and requires approval from College Events and the Library Director for its use as an event area.
cards.access_notes: For event use, approval from the Office of College Events and Director of the Library is required.

cards.title: Cabell Room 406
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Use the tables for a larger collaborative review or project meeting. Keep the setup within the room’s stated 24-person table capacity.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor Bortz Library room with tables for up to 24 people.
cards.evidence_claim: The College’s event planning guide lists Cabell Room 406 with a maximum seating capacity of 24 around its tables.
cards.access_notes: Follow College event-space procedures; food and drink are allowed under the guide’s listed conditions.

cards.title: Fourth-Floor Lecture Area
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Use this presentation-ready area when your study group needs to rehearse slides or view media. Request use through the College process.
cards.short_summary: A fourth-floor presentation area with shades, projection, sound, and rolling desks.
cards.evidence_claim: The College lists Bortz Library’s Fourth Floor Lecture Area with room-darkening shades, a presenter workstation, ceiling-mounted projector, sound system, and rolling classroom desks.
cards.access_notes: Available by request; the guide states a standard setup of rolling classroom desks for 30.

cards.title: Fuqua Technology Commons Mac Lab
cards.subtitle: Walter M. Bortz III Library
cards.notes: Use the Mac Lab when coursework needs a campus workstation or high-quality scanning. Ask FTC staff for help with the available scanning equipment.
cards.short_summary: A Bortz Library technology workspace with an open Mac lab and scanning resources.
cards.evidence_claim: Hampden-Sydney identifies the Fuqua Technology Commons as housing the campus’s only open Mac computer lab; its scanning guide places a flatbed scanner in the FTC Mac Lab.
cards.access_notes: Located in Bortz Library; consult FTC staff for scanner assistance and follow current campus access policies.
